record.title: Equatorial Guinea extends Cameroon land closure beyond independence holiday
record.consequences: Traders and merchandise stranded; AFP interviewed an Ebebiyin vendor reporting sharp income loss, without generalising the figure.
record.relationship: Separate 2019 episode after SC 25 phased 2017–2019 restrictions; do not assume continuous closure across reopening.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; current status not inferred
record.official_rationale: Initial closure reported ahead of independence celebrations; continuing closure not explained by authorities
record.context: A holiday closure officially began on 11 October 2019 and remained in place at the 22 October AFP interviews and 31 October local roundup. A 3 April 2020 report still describes suspension of ordinary passenger and goods movement dating from 11 October, predating COVID closures by neighbouring states.
record.uncertainty: The French AFP version explicitly reports 11 October 2019 as the official closure date. No reopening was recovered; a 3 April 2020 local report still describes suspension of people and goods. Equatorial Guinea supplied no explanation for the extension. A Cameroonian governor’s speculation about security is not coded as causation. Continuous universal closure is not established.
